cells.tense: You are here at the edge of something undecided, and you know what is ending.
cells.ask: Pick one thing that is over. Say out loud that it is over, and what that gives back to you.
cells.core:
Something in you is completing, and you are not fighting it. You can feel which parts of your life have run their course, and you let them finish instead of propping them up. That clearing is what makes room; you already trust it, so you are not scrambling to fill the space.

The fairness in this is the quiet kind — you know what you have given and what it cost, and you are not keeping score about it. Underneath, something is getting even. What is done is being let go of at the same pace it is being honored. That is the balance: you can name one thing and let it rest.
cells.sheetLine: You can let a thing finish without calling it a loss.
cells.verb: letting what is finished end so something else can start
cells.place: the open room where nothing has been decided yet

cells.tense: You will be the one who ends it, and you are already bracing for that future.
cells.ask: Finish one ordinary thing you started, all the way to its end. Then wait a day before starting anything new.
cells.core:
You keep getting ahead of the ending. Some part of the story still has life in it, and you are already picturing the clean break — what you will say, how free it will feel. That picture keeps you one step out of the present, and the present is the only place any of this gets to be real.

What you call liberation is often something else wearing its coat. Ending early feels like courage because it is quick, but the fear stays — it just moves to the next thing ahead of you. Nothing you cut away reaches the part of you that is bracing. That part needs to be met where it is, not outpaced.
cells.sheetLine: You end things early and call the quickness freedom.
cells.verb: letting what is finished end so something else can start

cells.tense: You were loyal to something that finished a long time ago, and you are still there.
cells.ask: Leave one thing undone today. Say to yourself that it is finished, then close the drawer, the page, or the door.
cells.core:
Nothing is being allowed to end. The thing that is over is being kept warm by habit, and calling that loyalty does not change what it is. What is done has not been put down. The waiting is not neutral — it takes up room that would otherwise be free for something else.

The knack for letting something finish has gone quiet, not disappeared. It comes back the same way it left, through small ends rather than large ones — through things that take almost no courage, only completion. Once one thing is finished, the pull toward what is next tends to wake up on its own. Nothing needs forcing. Something needs finishing.
cells.sheetLine: The thing is already over. You are keeping it warm.
cells.verb: letting what is finished end so something else can start
cells.place: the open room where nothing has been decided yet

cells.tense: Something is ending in you right now, and the pen is down while it happens.
cells.ask: Write down one thing you have said goodbye to this year without noticing. Read it back once, as a fact.
cells.core:
Something in you has been ending for a while, and you have not been treating it as an ending. The clearing is happening anyway — in what you no longer reach for, what you stopped bringing up, what quietly dropped away. From the outside it looks like drift. It is not drift; it is change running without a witness.

What you are actually doing is letting go in pieces while calling it nothing in particular. The shape of your days has already shifted around that ending. Saying it out loud changes almost nothing out there, and gives back the fact that you are the one who did it. Not the drift. You.
cells.sheetLine: The end already happened. You just have not called it that.
cells.verb: letting what is finished end so something else can start
cells.place: the open room where nothing has been decided yet

attempts.check: The draft claimed the ending 'was needed at the time' and that stale room 'costs you the room you would need for anything else' — the record says nothing about how the earlier choice looked or what holding on has cost, so both go. A reader could fairly say nothing has visibly ended and this is all inward; the asks survive that, because naming one thing as finished is useful work whether or not my read is right. The sentence serving me over them was the symmetrical 'the door is behind you and you are still standing in front of it' — it sounded wise and named nothing a person could check, and the refrain was the machine's tell, so it's gone.
